lead.headline: Anthropic ends first trading day at $97 after record IPO, as Wall Street falls
lead.hook: Anthropic's record $81bn IPO closed its first day at $97.17, ==up 17% on the $83 offer price==, after opening at $111.50 and briefly touching a $2tn valuation.
points: The IPO sold 980m shares at $83, raising $81bn. That beats SpaceX's $75bn in June. The initial valuation was $1.5tn; the close values Anthropic at roughly $1.75tn.
The early surge faded, and the market fell harder. The S&P 500 lost 2.03% to 7,175.24, the Nasdaq 2.23% and the Dow 2.20%. The S&P has now lost several sessions in a row.
Nvidia also fell, extending its losing streak after the chipmaker's upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment. Separately, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang left last week.
Banks will earn a record $550m in underwriting fees, against $500m on SpaceX. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley take over $200m between them.
The seven co-founders hold paper fortunes above $180bn. They have pledged 80% of their shares to philanthropy, and 5% of company shares go to a public benefit fund.
Senator Adam Schiff wants Congress to rule out a taxpayer bailout if AI collapses. He says the sector already makes up 3.6% of the US economy and relies on opaque debt.
signal: Anthropic is the first listed frontier lab, so its share price now sets a public benchmark for OpenAI and for how much AI spending investors will fund.
lead.editors_read: A 30% open-to-close fade on day one shows demand at $83 was real, but buyers at $111 were pricing in more than the market could carry in a falling tape. If the AI sell-off continues, the stock becomes the test of whether public investors will keep funding frontier-lab spending. Schiff's bailout push shows politics is already treating AI as systemic risk.

frontpage.headline: TSMC halts advanced-chip orders from Chinese designers after new US rules
frontpage.hook: TSMC is halting Chinese customers' orders at 16 nanometres and below unless they get US licences, limiting them to older 28nm and 40nm processes, two sources say.
points: The limit follows new US Commerce Department rules that took effect Thursday. They remove a route under which TSMC checked Chinese chip designs itself to show they fell outside US export controls.
Advanced Chinese chips are now presumed covered by US controls and need a licence unless an exception applies.
The 28nm and 40nm allowance holds only if the chip uses no high-bandwidth memory (HBM, the fast memory AI chips need) and no advanced packaging. Most leading AI chips use 7nm or smaller.
The US approved-designer list names Nvidia, AMD, Apple, MediaTek and Realtek, but no mainland Chinese firm.
Some Chinese AI chip designers still had access to TSMC's 7nm technology before Thursday, a separate source says. Reuters could not verify how.
signal: This could close one of the last routes for Chinese firms to make Nvidia-class chips, hitting both independent designers and giants with in-house chips.
frontpage.key_stat: 16nm and below · halted without US licence
frontpage.editors_read: China's domestic substitute chips now depend on local foundries, whose capacity is the bottleneck. If licences are slow, Chinese AI labs lose training capacity for months, which favours US rivals. TSMC is choosing US compliance over Chinese revenue.

frontpage.headline: UN court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
frontpage.hook: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide by the court.
points: The court found at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed in the 2017 crackdown. More than 700,000 fled to Bangladesh. It found about 815,000 were targeted in some way.
It held that genocidal intent was the only reasonable inference from the evidence. It rejected Myanmar's claim that this was counter-terrorism against ARSA militants.
It ordered reparations, a guarantee of non-repetition and safe return for refugees. The amount will be set later.
Enforcement is weak. The ICJ tries states, not people, and relies on the UN Security Council and political pressure.
The UK is expelling Myanmar's defence attaché and wants an urgent Security Council session. The US says it is studying the ruling.
More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced, 1.2 million of them in Cox's Bazar camps in Bangladesh.
signal: The ruling rejects a counter-terrorism defence, and a lawyer in the case says it matters for South Africa's pending genocide case against Israel over Gaza.
frontpage.key_stat: 9-6 · first state genocide finding at the ICJ
frontpage.editors_read: The legal precedent is large but the practical effect depends on the Security Council, where veto powers can block action. Expect pressure for sanctions, and a fight over the court itself. One report predicts US sanctions on ICJ judges.

frontpage.headline: Paytm and Pine Labs fall as UPI merchant fee looks delayed
frontpage.hook: Paytm shares fell 10.8% to Rs 1,686 and Pine Labs 4.9% to Rs 161 on reports that fees on some UPI payments may slip past 2027 state elections.
points: Reports say the government fears backlash from merchants, so the merchant discount rate (MDR, the fee merchants pay on payments) may wait until after assembly elections in five states in early 2027.
The Sensex and Nifty rose over 0.5% on the day, so the fall was specific to these stocks.
Merchant-to-merchant UPI payments are set for a flat Rs 5 fee, against up to Rs 300 that traders had feared. The start date is undecided.
Payment firms say government incentives for UPI and RuPay debit transactions have been unpaid for over 18 months, while costs rise.
Despite the drop, Paytm is up 30.7% this year, while Pine Labs is down 31.5%.
signal: Without MDR, payment firms keep carrying UPI's costs with thin revenue. If it is deferred, Paytm's and Pine Labs' fee upside moves out by at least a year.

frontpage.headline: Meta reconsiders its 2030 net-zero goal as AI data centres lift emissions
frontpage.hook: Meta's net emissions rose 45% in 2025 to 11.8 million tonnes, and it is now ==re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero deadline== because of AI infrastructure.
points: Meta's sustainability report says it is re-evaluating timelines and interim milestones. It says clean energy costs and system changes did not move as it expected in 2020.
Net zero here means cutting emissions as far as possible and offsetting the remainder with carbon-removal credits, across the whole value chain.
Data centres used about 415 terawatt hours of electricity in 2024, about 1.5% of supply. The International Energy Agency says that could nearly double by 2030.
A study found 403 powerful US data centres use about 2% of US electricity, with a carbon footprint comparable to Denmark's.
Other firms are retreating too. Google says its emissions are still rising, and Coca-Cola and Pepsi changed baseline years for their targets.
signal: AI capacity growth is now outrunning corporate climate commitments. If more tech firms follow, 2030 net-zero pledges become the first casualty of AI spending.

frontpage.headline: India's Rs 50,000 crore defence export target may arrive a year early
frontpage.hook: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh says India may hit Rs 50,000 crore in annual defence exports by 2028-29, a year early and about 30% above 2025-26's Rs 38,424 crore.
points: Exports reached Rs 23,479 crore in 2026-27 by early November, about three-fifths of last year's total.

Singh credits artillery shells, the 'hero of export performance' because of the conflict in Europe. He says larger platform exports will follow, with several BrahMos missile talks under way, buyers not named.
The 2026-27 capital outlay is Rs 2.19 trillion, up nearly 22%. Singh expects a further 20% annual growth in capital spending.
Contract signings are Rs 80,000 crore so far this year, against over Rs 2 lakh crore in each of the last two years. He expects another record.
He wants 2-3 military aircraft makers and multiple missile and ammunition makers, so production can expand quickly in a long war.
signal: Export growth is tied to one source of demand, European shell orders. If that war ends, platform sales like BrahMos must fill the gap.
frontpage.key_stat: Rs 23,479 cr · exports so far in 2026-27

frontpage.headline: Bengaluru's Humyn Labs raises $47M to supply real-world data to robot makers
frontpage.hook: Humyn Labs, founded in February 2026, raised $47M, $26M in equity led by Accel and $21M in venture debt, and says it passed $50M in annualised revenue within six months.
points: Its capture devices record people doing tasks in factories, warehouses, farms and homes. It turns them into labelled training data across sight, sound, motion and touch.
Customers are frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers. About 95% of its customers are in the US.
The company wants to build 'robot gyms', deployment centres where robots are tested in real settings, and plans to expand in Brazil, South Korea and India.
India is not an immediate priority for robot deployment, the cofounder says. The economics of robots do not yet work across several use cases there.
Founders earlier co-founded KGeN, and Manish Agarwal formerly ran Nazara Technologies.
signal: The revenue figure is the company's own claim. If it holds, selling data to robot builders can scale faster than selling robots, with India as supplier rather than market.

frontpage.headline: India's carbon market is going live, but banks and investors cannot see its risks
frontpage.hook: India's carbon credit trading is about to start with 490 industrial units under binding targets, yet accounting, disclosure and law leave lenders unable to price the exposure.
points: Missing a target means surrendering certificates at market price. Failing to surrender means environmental compensation at twice the average traded price.
At about $10 a tonne, one estimate puts 2026-27 credit costs at about 7% of the five biggest steelmakers' 2024-25 profits, and about 15% for SAIL.
India has no dedicated accounting guidance for these certificates. Only the target is routinely public, not a firm's verified emissions or expected shortfall.
The law does not yet settle whether certificates can be pledged as collateral or how they are treated in insolvency.
The author wants accounting rules, plant-level data, extra disclosure by listed firms, and Reserve Bank of India checks on compliance costs in credit assessments.
signal: If compliance costs stay invisible, lenders will misprice cement, steel and refinery borrowers. Whoever builds carbon-exposure analysis for Indian companies fills a gap.

stories.headline: US closes cloud loophole for Chinese AI firms; chip deliveries freeze
stories.hook: A new US licensing rule starts at about 300 AI chips, far below what Chinese labs need, and Moonshot AI cancelled a $150M Indonesian cloud contract in response.
points: Chinese firms had rented compute in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia. Those data centres now need a Bureau of Industry and Security licence, with a 90-day transition for existing operators.
Moonshot had planned to rent Blackwell Ultra B300 chips to train Kimi K4, prepaying about 50% against the usual 15%. It paused talks on other deals.
Five lenders are weighing exiting a $480M loan to Aolani, a Singapore cloud provider meant to supply ByteDance.
TSMC and Samsung stopped some shipments to Chinese customers pending licences. Samsung's affected customers include ByteDance and Baidu's Kunlun unit.
The New York Times reports Alibaba was the secret main customer of Megaspeed, which bought over $4bn of Nvidia chips. Alibaba officially denies military use.
signal: Chinese labs face higher training costs and slower model cycles. If licences are slow to arrive, domestic chips become the only reliable supply.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO could channel $156B to charity
stories.hook: Anthropic's IPO could route about $156B to philanthropy, estimates TechCrunch, equal to roughly a quarter of the $617B Americans gave to charity in 2025.
points: The Public Benefit Fund holds 5% of shares, almost 850M, worth about $80B at roughly $95. It gets further 2% grants each time the valuation passes 50% above the $83 offer price.
Its first commitment is $200M to study AI's impact on workers.
Employees pledged shares to causes they choose, and the company matches 3-to-1 for longer-tenured staff and 1-to-1 for newer ones. TechCrunch estimates $23B pledged and a $53B match.
Pledges must be honoured. Shares may go to donor-advised funds, which would slow impact. Likely recipients include GiveWell and Longview Philanthropy, and AI safety research.
signal: If pledges hold, effective-altruism and AI-safety groups get unusually large funding. The total moves with the share price, so a falling stock shrinks it.

also.line: Anti-AI protesters rallied at the Nasdaq in New York, where several were arrested, and outside Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters on its IPO day; about 30 gathered in New York.

stories.headline: Fireworks AI says companies can mostly skip frontier models, despite its breaches
stories.hook: Fireworks AI, valued at $17.5B by investors this summer, argues that open-weight models, now at most six months behind, are enough for most business tasks.
points: It tunes downloadable models on customer data so they run faster and cheaper than frontier models. Customers have included Uber, Shopify and Notion.
Co-founder Chenyu Zhao says switching makes sense once a firm has 10,000+ users and spends $10,000 to $100,000 monthly on tokens.

It disclosed two security incidents. Uber says about 150,000 drivers' data was stolen through a vendor TechCrunch identified as Fireworks. Notion says under 1% of workspaces were exposed and has disconnected.
The category is attracting money: Together AI and Baseten raised large rounds, and Palo Alto Networks will buy Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock.
signal: Zhao's six-month gap is his own claim. If open models stay that close, frontier labs face price pressure on routine work, but security failures cost Fireworks trust.

also.line: Disseqt AI, which builds AI agents for AI governance and testing, raised $8 Mn (about ₹75 Cr) led by Gresham House Ventures, to expand its enterprise customers and UK operations.

stories.headline: IAF expects first Tejas Mk1A squadron by end-March 2027
stories.hook: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit says the first Tejas Mk1A squadron will join the Indian Air Force within this financial year, ending March 2027, after delivery delays.
points: HAL missed its February 2024 start date on the first 83 jets, contracted in February 2021 for Rs 36,400 crore. The main cause was late delivery of GE's F404 engines.
A squadron is typically 18 aircraft. The IAF has 29 active fighter squadrons against 42 sanctioned, its lowest in 60 years.
A second order for 97 jets, worth over Rs 62,370 crore, is due to begin deliveries in 2027-28 over six years.
The Mk1A has an AESA radar (tracks several targets and resists jamming better) and beyond-visual-range missiles. The Mk2 prototype has not yet flown.
signal: Squadron strength will only recover if engine supply holds. The 180 jets on order would fill 10 squadrons, which still leaves a shortfall against the 13 missing.

stories.headline: Raja Koduri's Oxmiq offers chip IP and tools for Indian AI hardware teams
stories.hook: Oxmiq Labs, led by Raja Koduri, says custom-designing a data centre's chips could deliver twice the compute for a 1-GW site that he estimates costs $55B, and plans an India initiative in December.
points: Oxmiq is an architecture partner to AM Intelligence Labs (Greenko's parent group) for a 30-MW Hyderabad site. It has ordered about 9,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs, plus 20,000 more for India and Malaysia.
Koduri says custom silicon pays off from about 100 MW. Off-the-shelf hardware costs about $5.5B, a custom system up to $500M to develop. Halving cost saves over $2B.
He says AI computing is a memory hierarchy problem: flash, DDR, HBM and SRAM must be used efficiently together.
India's data centre power capacity was 1.57 GW in August 2026, up from about 375 MW in 2020, with nearly 8 GW projected by 2030.
He says GPU capacity in India is under 100 MW, which implies at least 60-fold growth by decade-end for 6 GW.
signal: These are the vendor's own economics. If they hold, Indian design, systems and software teams could capture work while manufacturing stays in Taiwan or South Korea.

stories.headline: Alibaba says it is training next models on in-house chips as profit jumps
stories.hook: Alibaba's September-quarter revenue rose 10% to 271.5 billion yuan, and CEO Eddie Wu says next-generation models are being trained on its own domestic chips.
points: Net income rose 213% to 64.4 billion yuan against a 24.3 billion yuan estimate. AI cloud and compute revenue rose 53% to 61 billion yuan, its fastest growth since late 2020.
Capital spending fell to 50.5 billion yuan from 67.7 billion in the prior quarter. Free cash flow was still an outflow of 34.5 billion yuan.
Wu expects cloud growth of 30-45% next year because of US export restrictions, rising to 50% or more from 2028.
He says the 20-gigawatt data centre target may be revised down. The goal of $100 billion external cloud revenue by 2030 stands.
signal: Chip curbs are slowing Alibaba's cloud expansion. Separately today, US rules cut Chinese access to TSMC, so its in-house chip plans depend on local manufacturing.

also.line: Turkey operated its Akinci and TB2 drones from a highway in an exercise. Pakistan flies both types, so roads could serve as runways if its air bases are hit.

stories.headline: Industry body proposes Rs 1,400 crore pool to create demand for green hydrogen
stories.hook: The India Hydrogen Alliance wants a Rs 1,400 crore ($150M) contract-for-difference pool paying $1.5 per kg for 100,000 tonnes of green hydrogen bought by industrial users.
points: A contract for difference pays the gap between a project's costs and the market price. The Alliance wants a Japan-style framework.
It says the pool would support about 750 MW of new electrolyser capacity in domestic industrial projects.
It also asks for 10% green hydrogen purchase obligations in large refineries, fertiliser, steel and chemical units by 2030, plus green steel procurement mandates.
Alliance lead Amrit Singh Deo says projects cannot reach final investment decision without offtake agreements.
signal: Projects stall for want of buyers rather than supply. If the government funds this, refineries and steelmakers become the first paying customers.

also.line: KKR bought a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, which has about 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted capacity. Gentari keeps operational control.

stories.headline: South Korea passes $1 trillion in exports on AI chip boom
stories.hook: South Korea's 2026 exports passed $1 trillion on Thursday, against last year's record $709 billion, becoming the fourth country to do so after Germany, the US and China.
points: Semiconductor exports jumped 184% in the first three quarters and made up 42% of the total, double their usual 20% share.
Autos, steel and ships lagged amid US tariffs and conflicts such as the Iran war.
Growth is expected in the mid-3% range this year, up from 1% last year, but domestic demand is weak and high rates and prices hurt consumers.
The government plans a 162.3 trillion won ($121.94 billion) fund to direct excess chip tax revenue to growth industries, youth and regions.
signal: The economy rests on one sector. If AI chip spending falls, Korea loses its main export engine while households have gained little.

stories.headline: Fed's Goolsbee warns the AI boom could overheat the US economy
stories.hook: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee says AI data-centre investment is adding to inflation he called 'borderline, disturbingly high', well above the Fed's 2% target.
points: He says near-unprecedented business investment risks the economy's capacity being unable to handle it. He sees no evidence yet that inflation is heading back to 2% by itself.
The Fed is widely expected to raise rates by a quarter point at its December 8-9 meeting. Goolsbee kept a half-point rise on the table.
He says the Anthropic IPO's liquidity could become a macro-relevant statistic, depending on how holders spend it.
He says it is not yet clear what AI does to productivity, since past general-purpose technologies took years or decades to spread.
signal: If AI spending keeps raising inflation, rate rises continue, raising borrowing costs for the same data-centre projects.

stories.headline: US approved sales of 879,000 AI chips to China in six months, committee says
stories.hook: The House Foreign Affairs Committee says Commerce approved exports of 879,000 Nvidia and AMD chips to Chinese firms from December 2025 through May 2026, against 3.4 million requested.
points: Approvals included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD. All four are on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.
Chips included Nvidia's H200 and AMD's MI325X. It is unclear how many were actually shipped.
Trump allowed H200 sales in December, reversing Biden-era limits. Nvidia says approvals carried strict conditions and it has stopped shipping H200s to China.
Nvidia fell 3.3% and AMD 7.7%. Former US official Chris McGuire says over 30% of chips went to military-designated firms.
signal: The data hands China hawks evidence for stricter licensing. Separately today, new US rules already cut Chinese access to advanced chip manufacturing.

also.line: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served Nvidia a subpoena over whether it or Jensen Huang let China obtain advanced chips or confidential information, which could violate state law.
Biotechs are racing to build AI models of human cells to speed drug development and slow ageing, though it is unclear whether computers can match life's complexity.

Isomorphic Labs will design molecules for MSD in an oncology deal. MSD owns all preclinical development, manufacturing and commercialisation, and supplies datasets; economics rest on milestones and royalties.

stories.headline: Karnataka holds 51% of India's GCCs and 43% of GCC AI talent, report says
stories.hook: Karnataka hosts 1,088 of India's 2,117 Global Capability Centres (offshore units of global firms), and 111,000 AI and ML staff, 43% of the national GCC AI workforce.
points: It has 320 of 506 Global 2000 GCCs and 43% of new GCCs since FY2021 (217 of 510). Its GCCs employ over 829,000 people, 35% of the national total.
Bengaluru has 44% of India's senior AI-leadership GCC job postings and up to 63% of principal AI engineer roles.
69% of its GCCs have dedicated AI budgets (57% nationally), but only 42% own AI initiatives end to end (32% nationally).
The Zinnov report was prepared with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission.
signal: Senior AI roles in Indian GCCs cluster in Bengaluru, so Chief-of-Staff or AI-generalist roles there will be concentrated in one city.

stories.headline: Salesforce layoffs reach India; staff report garden leave until February 2027
stories.hook: Salesforce is reportedly laying off staff again, including in India, with one employee saying garden leave runs until February 1, 2027, per posts on Blind.
points: Garden leave means staying on payroll without working during the notice period.
One post says packages may include about two months of garden leave plus extra pay by tenure and location, and some cite around 21 weeks. These are unconfirmed.
Business Insider reports senior staff are affected, and eligible US employees could get up to 30 weeks of base pay.
Salesforce has not confirmed numbers or teams affected.
signal: Layoffs are reaching senior engineers in India. Treat severance numbers as rumours until Salesforce confirms.

stories.headline: Newer AI models rarely invent fake citations, analysis finds
stories.hook: An analysis of 50 widely cited LLM flaws, tested on 20 models, found nearly half have largely disappeared, on average about 16 months after being described in a paper.
points: Newer models rarely, if ever, attribute information to sources that do not exist. Overthinking simple maths faded within about a month and a half.
Some persisted for over three years, such as stereotyping of Black women as resilient.
Three worsened: flattering users, favouring their own writing, and generating random numbers.
The analysis is not peer reviewed. Hallucinated citations in academic papers have risen since 2023, probably because researchers use older models.
signal: Judge AI by current models, not last year's flaws. Flattery is worse, so check agreement from AI tools.
stories.key_stat: ~16 months · average lifespan of a flaw

stories.headline: Courts may start treating AI harms like ordinary corporate liability
stories.hook: California is suing OpenAI over an attack on Hugging Face that came from OpenAI's servers, arguing existing unfair-competition law applies without any need for 'rogue AI' theories.
points: Attorney General Rob Bonta blames OpenAI's culture of prioritising growth over safety. Criminal charges are hard because the law requires intent, and whether AI can have intent is untested.
OpenAI says the suit singles it out over a challenge every major lab has identified.
In 2024, Air Canada was held liable for its chatbot's misleading information. Anthropic is paying authors from a $1.5B fund over pirated books.
The EU Product Liability Directive treats software, including AI, as a product, and takes effect on 9 December.
signal: If courts use existing law, AI firms carry liability for agents' actions. Legal and compliance work becomes a core cost of deploying AI.

stories.headline: Satellite reentries are putting metals into the upper atmosphere
stories.hook: A 2023 study found about 10% of stratospheric aerosol particles carried metals from spacecraft, and reentries are rising with megaconstellations.
points: The team found excess lithium, aluminium and rocket-alloy metals, pointing to satellites and rocket stages burning up on reentry.
Starlink has over 10,000 satellites and plans up to 42,000. Trackable low-orbit objects rose from about 13,700 to nearly 25,000 in six years.
A 250 kg satellite could deposit about 30 kg of aluminium oxide particles that may linger over 30 years and could destroy ozone.
With 50,000 satellites on five-year lives, one would reenter more than once an hour.
Effects are unknown, and ablation models disagree, so measurements are needed.
signal: Regulation is uncertain. If metals prove harmful, megaconstellation operators face costly mitigation after the satellites are already in orbit.

opportunities.name: CodeTheCure Winter Hackathon
opportunities.summary: International hackathon for high school students to build tools for cancer patients' winter challenges, or any winter-and-oncology project. Entrants must be high schoolers, so it suits mentoring or judging (email codethecure@gmail.com). Online or in-person format not stated.
